abate.d: v. to become less active, less intense, or less in amount

ameliorate.d: v. To improve or make better.

approximate.d: adj. Nearly accurate or close to.

arcane.d: adj. Mysterious or known by few.

adj. extremely plain
adj. stern and forbidding
adj. relating to self-denial

He lived in a small, austere cabin in the middle of the woods.

An austere lifestyle, like that of monks, isn’t for everybody.

avoid.d: v. To stay away from or prevent.

commercialization.d: n. The process of making something a business.

complexity.d: n. The state of being intricate or complicated.

diminish.d: v. To decrease in size or importance.

disastrous.d: adj. Causing great harm or failure.

discount.d: v. To disregard or reduce in value.

discretion.d: n. The ability to make responsible choices.

dismiss.d: v. To reject or send away.

distressed.d: adj. Suffering from anxiety or pain.

expansion.d: n. The act of increasing in size or scope.

expensive.d: adj. Costing a lot of money.

fruitless.d: adj. Failing to achieve desired results.

hibernation.d: n. A state of dormancy or deep sleep.

hinder.d: v. To obstruct or slow progress.

hypothesize.d: v. To form a theory or assumption.

imaginative.d: adj. Creative and full of new ideas.

imitation.d: n. A copy or replica of something.

immune.d: adj. Resistant to disease or harm.

impartial.e: Judges must always remain impartial during a trial.

inexplicable.e: My uncle's sudden departure from the family reunion was inexplicable.

influence.d: n. The power to affect others.

insensible.e: The father was insensible to his children's boredom.

insignificant.d: adj. Too small or unimportant to matter.

intangible.d: adj. Not able to be touched or measured.

invent.e: Thomas Edison invented the incandescent light bulb.

lacking.d: adj. Not having enough of something.

latent.e: He had a latent talent for music.

misrepresent.d: v. To give a false impression.

novel.e: The doctor introduced a novel approach to hip surgery.

nuanced.e: His argument was well-developed and nuanced.

obligate.e: The contract obligates him to pay.

ornamental.e: The garden was filled with ornamental plants that helped beautify the space.

praise.d: v. To express approval or admiration.

relocate.e: The dentist relocated to a bigger office.

renounce.d: v. To give up or reject formally.
renounce.e: He renounced his citizenship after moving to a new country.

replenish.e: After we finished the lemonade, the hostess replenished the pitcher.

replicable.d: adj. Able to be copied or repeated.

representative.d: n. A person acting on behalf of others.
representative.e: The company's representative spoke at the meeting.

repress.d: v. To suppress or hold back.
repress.e: Although devastated, Jalen repressed his emotions.

reprieve.d: n. A temporary relief or delay.
reprieve.e: Because the defendant needed surgery, the judge granted a reprieve.

repudiate.e: She repudiated the accusation that she'd stolen money from the company.

resilient.e: Even after setbacks, the patient is very resilient.

resolve.e: The warring siblings eventually resolved their differences.

responsive.e: The team wanted to improve and was very responsive to feedback.

restore.d: v. To bring back to original condition.
restore.e: The architecture team carefully restored the old house.

restrain.d: v. To hold back or limit.
restrain.e: Even though Tom was furious, he restrained his anger.

retain.d: v. To keep or hold onto.
retain.e: I use this pitcher to retain water for my herb garden.

retaliate.d: v. To respond to an attack.
retaliate.e: After Celia yelled at Dom, he retaliated with a counterattack.

reticent.d: adj. Reluctant to share one's thoughts or feelings; reserved
reticent.e: My neighbor is so reticent I never know what she really thinks of anything.

rousing.e: The speaker gave a rousing speech that brought the audience to its feet.

rudimentary.e: The little boy only has a rudimentary understanding of math.

sanction.e: The government sanctioned the project so construction will start soon.

sanguine.e: He remained sanguine despite repeated setbacks.

saturate.d: v. To soak or fill completely.
saturate.e: The sponge was saturated with water.

scorn.d: v. to look down on with disdain
scorn.e: It’s difficult for me not to scorn those who use improper grammar.

scrutinize.e: I'm going to have my lawyer scrutinize the contract.

secretive.e: He was secretive about his plans for Valentine's Day.

sensitive.e: She is very sensitive to criticism.

simulate.e: The pilot simulated an emergency landing.

sincerity.d: n. The quality of being genuine.
sincerity.e: His sincerity was evident in his speech.

skeptical.e: The teacher was skeptical of the student's claim that the dog ate her homework.

sophisticated.e: The building's design was intricate and sophisticated.

span.d: n. The extent or length of something.
span.e: The Golden Gate Bridge has a long span.

sparingly.d: adv. insufficiently, meagerly, or in a restricted manner
sparingly.e: Due to my blood pressure, I must eat salt sparingly.

speculate.e: He speculated about the outcome of the soccer match.

spurious.e: The claims were spurious and therefore thrown out in court.

stark.d: adj. Very plain; devoid of any details or features
stark.e: Looking out at the stark landscape, I felt a keen sense of isolation.

strenuously.e: She strenuously denied the accusations against her.

sturdily.e: The chair was sturdily built and had no chance of breaking.

stymie.e: The restoration project was stymied by a lack of funds.

substantial.e: Jackie made a substantial donation to her alma mater.

subtle.d: adj. Hard to detect or analyze
subtle.e: The author gave a subtle hint as to who the murderer was.

succumb.d: v. To give in or surrender.
succumb.e: He succumbed to the temptation to eat the entire bag of gummy bears.

superficial.e: The candidate struggled to answer questions about policy because his knowledge was superficial.

supplement.e: She supplemented her income by starting a side hustle.

surmise.e: He surmised the answer based on context clues.

surpass.d: v. To exceed or go beyond.
surpass.e: She surpassed expectations by winning the national spelling bee.

surrender.d: v. To give up or yield.
surrender.e: The weakened army surrendered to the enemy.

susceptible.e: With his weakened immune system, Marcelo is susceptible to illness.

synchronization.d: n. The process of coordinating events.
synchronization.e: The synchronization of lights helped traffic flow.

tentative.d: adj. Uncertain or not fully decided.
tentative.e: Our plans are tentative and may change.

tenuous.e: His argument was tenuous at best.

theoretical.d: adj. Based on theory rather than practice.
theoretical.e: The idea remains theoretical until tested.

theory.d: n. A system of ideas intended to explain something.
theory.e: Einstein's theory of relativity changed physics.

thoughtfulness.e: Her thoughtfulness made her a great friend.

tranquil.e: The lake was tranquil at sunset.

transform.d: v. To change in form or appearance.
transform.e: The caterpillar transformed into a butterfly.

ubiquitous.e: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in society.

uncontroversial.d: adj. Not likely to cause disagreement.
uncontroversial.e: The decision was uncontroversial and widely accepted.

undeniable.e: Simone Biles' talent as a gymnast is undeniable.

underscore.e: The report underscored the importance of safety.

unimportant.e: The details were unimportant to the main issue.

unintended.e: The side effects of the medication were unintended.

universal.e: The desire for love is universal.

unobtrusive.e: The waitress did her best to be unobtrusive while clearing the table.

unoriginal.e: His speech was unoriginal and predictable.

unpredictable.e: The weather in winter can often be unpredictable.

validate.d: v. To confirm the accuracy of something.
validate.e: The test results validated his hypothesis.

variable.e: The weather is highly variable in spring.

verisimilitude.d: n. The appearance of being true or real.
verisimilitude.e: The novel’s verisimilitude made it compelling.

vigilance.d: n. The action of keeping careful watch.
vigilance.e: Constant vigilance is needed for security.

vital.e: It is vital that you respond by the deadline.

volatile.d: adj. Liable to change rapidly and unpredictably; easily evaporated (in scientific contexts)
volatile.e: My uncle's mood is very volatile, so we never know how he's going to react.

waive.d: v. To give up a right or claim voluntarily.
waive.e: He waived his right to an attorney.

warranted.e: The decision was warranted by the evidence.

widespread.d: adj. Found or occurring over a large area.
